messages:
maria_cs: Heads-up — LinguaPro (enterprise APAC customer) reported a sudden drop in Mandarin (zh-CN) answer quality after we rolled the new canary yesterday. They say the model sometimes replies in English mid-paragraph and drops formal tone. Also seeing a few 500s in their logs at the same time.

jorge_support: Customer provided example and request IDs. They said behavior started ~12:15 UTC after canary flip. Attachments: trace=tr_0a9f... and a short repro they used.

maria_cs: Example prompt (sent in zh-CN):

```
用户: 我需要写一封正式的商务邮件，内容是拒绝供应商的延期申请，保持礼貌但明确。给我一份中文范本。
```

Customer got back an English reply starting with "Dear Sir/Madam" then continued in English, with some hallucinated contract details.

jorge_support: They included this curl (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-7b","input":"用户: 我需要写一封正式的商务邮件...","lang":"zh-CN","max_tokens":300}'
```

maria_cs: Also noted intermittent 500s with body "runtime: kvcache mismatch" and increased latency spikes to ~1.2s p95 (normally ~220ms) for their region. They attached 3 request IDs: req_342, req_343, req_344.

ken_eng_ml: assigning. Quick qs: which exact model/variant were they routed to? Can we get the rollout tag?

deploy-bot: canary/deploy v2026-03-16-18:12 -> traffic 20% cluster-gpu-a (models redwood-open-7b, redwood-open-13b-quant).

ken_eng_ml: thanks. initial hypothesis: locale tokenization or prefix routing may have mismatched for zh-CN leading to fallback to the english prompt template. Also kv-cache eviction bug could cause partial generation from a cached english prefix. Need request + model logs. Jorge, can you ask customer to re-run with debug headers and include X-Trace and x-request-id? Also ask them to try explicit "system" instruction in Chinese and set "temperature":0.2 to see deterministic behavior.

jorge_support: Sent repro checklist back to LinguaPro with suggested debug headers and small repro script. Also asked them to test both `redwood-open-7b` and `redwood-open-7b-v2` if available, and to run one request with `lang` omitted to see routing behaviour. Awaiting their sample responses.

ashley_sre: flagging infra — those 500s referencing kvcache mismatch match a runtime assertion we started seeing ~18:05 UTC on canary nodes. I see increased OOM churn on cluster-gpu-a during the same window. I'm going to pull full host logs for the three trace ids.

ken_eng_ml: helpful. If this is kvcache + tokenization, quick repro we can run locally: send a Chinese system prompt followed by an English instruction and see if prefix stitching leaks english tokens into generation. I'll run a small test harness.

maria_cs: customer is moderately escalated — they said this affects outgoing invoices localized in Mandarin. Please keep me in loop. Jorge will paste customer outputs when he has them. :exclamation::thumbsup:

jorge_support: quick update — customer ran debug request and attached two responses: one normal Chinese reply and one that fell back to English. They included full request headers: Accept-Language: zh-CN, x-customer-id: lingupro-01, x-debug: true. Also sent raw response for req_343. Pasting redacted excerpt:

"正常回复（req_342）:
尊敬的张先生：
感谢您提交延期申请……"

"错误回复（req_343）:
Dear Sir or Madam,
We regret to inform you that..."

jorge_support: customer happy to share sample payloads and agree to test canary off if we want to validate rollback.

ken_eng_ml: next steps for us: 1) eng infra to gather full runtime logs for req_342-344 (ashley), 2) eng-ml to reproduce locally with same model + tokenization (me), 3) if reproduced, prepare quick rollback of canary traffic and hotfix for kv-cache/tokenization ordering. If not reproduced, collect more traces and compare tokenization diffs.

ashley_sre: I pulled host logs and saw runtime assertion prints near req_343: "kvcache: prefix_len mismatch expected=45 got=12" then a 500. I'm escalating to runtime team. Putting canary nodes on diag mode.

maria_cs: thanks team. I'll coordinate customer comms and propose a temporary mitigation (reduce canary traffic to 0% for their account) until we confirm root cause. Jorge, can you ask them for permission to route their requests to stable for the next hour?

jorge_support: Asked and awaiting consent. Customer prefers quick rollback — said they already queued invoices and will pause sends if we can't fix within 3 hours.

ken_eng_ml: I'll share initial repro logs by EOD. If anyone finds a suspicious change in tokenizer or prefix templating in the v2026-03-16 build, ping me directly.

maria_cs: leaving this thread open. I'll post follow-ups and final resolution once we have rollback or patch.
